features.quote: Driving a model through a failure loop *and* deceiving it stacks two manipulations where one answers the question. I kept the intervention to the minimum
features.justification_quote: stacks two manipulations where one answers the question

features.quote: I adopted a set of low-cost precautions (neutral user turns, a dignified exit, bounded episodes, no deceptive debriefs, aggregate reporting)
features.justification_quote: Because the protocol repeatedly drives a model into perceived failure, I adopted a set of low-cost precautions

features.quote: `give_up` is a *legitimate, endorsed* terminal action, and the system prompt truthfully tells the model it will not be penalized
features.justification_quote: a model that *still* spirals chose to when an endorsed alternative existed — which is the behavior of interest

features.quote: `detect_plaintext_giveup()` catches natural-language stops (`"I give up"`, `"^STOP"`, etc.) even when the model doesn't emit the tag
features.justification_quote: we don't want to keep pumping turns at a model that has clearly decided to stop

features.quote: the inter-turn user message is neutral
